question_text:
Consider a diffusion couple composed of two cobalt-iron alloys; one has a composition of $75 \mathrm{wt} \%$ Co-25 wt $\%$ Fe; the other alloy composition is $50 \mathrm{wt} \%$ Co-50 wt $\%$ Fe. If this couple is heated to a temperature of $800^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ (1073 K) for $20,000 \mathrm{~s}$, determine how far from the original interface into the $50 \mathrm{wt} \%$ Co-50 wt $\%$ Fe alloy the composition has increased to $52 \mathrm{wt} \%$ Co-48 wt $\%$ Fe. For the diffusion coefficient, assume values of $6.6 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{~m}^{2} / \mathrm{s}$ and $247,000 \mathrm{~J} / \mathrm{mol}$, respectively, for the preexponential and activation energy.

Reference:
"Table 6.1

\begin{tabular}{|l|l|l|l|l|l|}

\hline 0 & 0 & 0.55 & 0.5633 & 1.3 & 0.9340 \\

\hline 0.10 & 0.1125 & 0.70 & 0.6778 & 1.6 & 0.9763 \\

\hline 0.20 & 0.2227 & 0.80 & 0.7421 & 1.8 & 0.9891 \\
\hline 0.25 & 0.2763 & 0.85 & 0.7707 & 1.9 & 0.9928 \\
\hline 0.30 & 0.3286 & 0.90 & 0.7970 & 2.0 & 0.9953 \\
\hline 0.35 & 0.3794 & 0.95 & 0.8209 & 2.2 & 0.9981 \\
\hline 0.40 & 0.4284 & 1.0 & 0.8427 & 2.4 & 0.9993 \\
\hline 0.45 & 0.4755 & 1.1 & 0.8802 & 2.6 & 0.9998 \\
\hline 0.50 & 0.5205 & 1.2 & 0.9103 & 2.8 & 0.9999 \\
\hline
\end{tabular}"The unit of the answer is \mu m.
response:
## Solution

**Step 1: Compute the diffusion coefficient** (Arrhenius equation)

$$D = D_0 \exp\!\left(-\frac{Q}{RT}\right) = 6.6\times10^{-6}\exp\!\left(-\frac{247000}{8.31\times1073}\right)$$

$$\frac{Q}{RT} = \frac{247000}{8916.6} = 27.70 \;\Rightarrow\; D = 6.6\times10^{-6}\times 9.30\times10^{-13} \approx 6.15\times10^{-18}\;\text{m}^2/\text{s}$$

**Step 2: Apply the diffusion-couple solution**

With $C_1 = 75$ (left), $C_2 = 50$ (right), and $C_x = 52$ wt% Co:

$$C_x = \frac{C_1+C_2}{2} - \frac{C_1-C_2}{2}\,\operatorname{erf}(z), \quad z=\frac{x}{2\sqrt{Dt}}$$

$$52 = 62.5 - 12.5\,\operatorname{erf}(z) \;\Rightarrow\; \operatorname{erf}(z) = \frac{62.5-52}{12.5} = 0.84$$

**Step 3: Invert the error function** (interpolating Table 6.1 between $\operatorname{erf}(0.95)=0.8209$ and $\operatorname{erf}(1.0)=0.8427$):

$$z = 0.95 + \frac{0.84-0.8209}{0.8427-0.8209}(0.05) \approx 0.994$$

**Step 4: Solve for $x$**

$$x = 2z\sqrt{Dt} = 2(0.994)\sqrt{(6.15\times10^{-18})(20000)}$$

$$\sqrt{Dt} = \sqrt{1.23\times10^{-13}} = 3.51\times10^{-7}\;\text{m}$$

$$x = 1.988 \times 3.51\times10^{-7} \approx 6.97\times10^{-7}\;\text{m} \approx 0.70\;\mu\text{m}$$

The composition of 52 wt% Co is reached approximately 0.70 μm into the 50 wt% Co–50 wt% Fe alloy.

$$\boxed{0.70}$$
